subject: Request: trial credit forgiveness for PoC delay - Chemlogic
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Anna Li <anna@chemlogic.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: trial credit forgiveness for PoC delay - Chemlogic

Hi Anna —

Thanks again for running the PoC with us. I wanted to flag that Chemlogic’s engineering team hit an unexpected blocker integrating our SDK with their legacy ingestion pipeline last week. The blocker has pushed back their test window by ~2–3 weeks.

Given the delay on their side (not product-related), they’re asking whether Redwood can provide a small credit to bridge the gap so they can complete validation once integration is unblocked. The ask is: a short-term credit (to cover ~200k tokens) and a 30-day trial extension so procurement has time to finalize SOW and entitlements.

Quick context:
- Initial PoC started 2026-12-01.
- Integration effort stalled 2026-12-24 due to parser edge cases in their ETL.
- Chemlogic expects engineering unblock by ~2027-01-10.

I’m happy to provide logs and the draft SOW for approval. Please let me know what documentation you need and whether we should route this through Partner Ops or Grants.

Best,
Rishi
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: integration-log-2026-12-27.txt (text), Chemlogic_SOW_v1.2.pdf (pdf)
From: Anna Li <anna@chemlogic.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Dec 2026 11:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: trial credit forgiveness for PoC delay - Chemlogic

Hi Rishi —

Thanks for the heads up and for sending the logs. Sorry to hear about the parser issue — we hit something similar with another customer last quarter. A couple quick asks:

1) Can you confirm the exact token estimate Chemlogic expects to consume during the resumed PoC (200k is fine if that’s accurate).
2) Please share the SOW you referenced so I can run this internally (procurement requires the SOW to approve any billing changes).

If you can send those two items I’ll put this in the queue for review. We try to be flexible for integration-induced delays.

—Anna
Senior Engineering Manager
Chemlogic
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Anna Li <anna@chemlogic.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Dec 2026 08:23:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: trial credit forgiveness for PoC delay - Chemlogic

Hi Anna / Rishi —

Appreciate the details here. We’ve reviewed the integration log Rishi attached. Proposed internal compromise to get Chemlogic back on track quickly:

- Grant a temporary credit equal to 150k tokens (one-time, non-recurring) to cover the immediate validation needs.
- Approve a 14-day automated trial extension tied to the SOW execution date (instead of an open-ended 30-day extension).

We can escalate to Partner Ops for a one-off exception if Chemlogic needs >150k or if procurement requires a longer extension; however, given fiscal controls, a 14-day extension plus a credit is the quickest path to keep momentum.

If acceptable to you, Rishi, I’ll loop in Marissa to prepare the grant and the invoice memo and will mark this as a priority for Partner Ops.

Thanks,
Monica
Head of MidMarket Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Anna Li <anna@chemlogic.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Dec 2026 12:11:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: trial credit forgiveness for PoC delay - Chemlogic

Monica —

Thanks for the quick review and proposal. I spoke to Chemlogic’s procurement and engineering leads this morning. Two notes:

- They really prefer a 30-day extension to give legal and procurement time to complete the SOW review — their holiday schedule extends approvals until mid-Jan.
- If we can’t extend to 30 days, they’ve asked that the temporary credit be bumped to 300k tokens so they can run more end-to-end tests in the compressed window.

I’m inclined to accept the 14-day + 150k for speed, but I want to confirm what flexibility we have before I push back. I’ve attached the SOW V1.2 and a trimmed integration log with reproducer notes.

If there’s a fast path to approve 30 days or 300k we should consider it — loss of momentum here makes conversion much harder.

Cheers,
Rishi
(attachments: Chemlogic_SOW_v1.2.pdf, integration-log-2026-12-27.txt)
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Anna Li <anna@chemlogic.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: trial credit forgiveness for PoC delay - Chemlogic

Rishi / Anna —

Thanks for the SOW and the clearer token numbers. I escalated to Partner Ops and Finance: preliminary approval to proceed with a one-time 300k token credit while legal completes the SOW, conditional on the following:

- Marissa to create a billing memo tying the credit to deal DL-2026-0891.
- A 30-day extension will be applied from the SOW execution date (we will record the execution date in HubSpot).
- Credit is non-refundable and limited to the PoC scope in the SOW.

Marissa — can you please process the credit grant and drop a DocuSign link for Chemlogic’s SOW? HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DL-2026-0891

Anna — appreciate your patience; we’ll aim to have the credit applied and the DocuSign in your inbox by tomorrow EOD PST.

Best,
Monica
Head of MidMarket Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
